title: Admission control KPIs + token-path trace dashboard for cross-region graceful degradation
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Purpose: Instrument and build a compact Grafana dashboard and alerting surface that focuses on admission-control KPIs and token-path traces to aid operators during cross-region capacity pressure and graceful degradation events. Goal is to provide actionable signals for when to (a) trigger regional circuit breakers, (b) adjust admission thresholds, and (c) initiate cross-region failover with clear attribution to token-level latency sources (e.g., KV cache misses, early-exit, queuing).

Scope:
- Add new metrics and enrich existing spans/tags: admission_decision, admission_reason, shard_id, region, kv_prefix_hit, kv_prefix_miss, queue_time_ms, token_emit_ms, model_variant, fallback_used.
- Implement a sampled token-path trace that captures per-token stage timings (receive -> admission -> routing -> backend_enqueue -> model_decode) at 0.5% global sampling and 5% for requests that experience admit/reject or latency > p95.
- Create an operator Grafana dashboard focused on: admission_rate (by region/shard), admit_reject_ratio with reasons, per-token p50/p95/p99 breakdown by stage, KV hit-rate heatmap, regional admission delta (primary vs backup), circuit_breaker_trip_rate, and synthetic failover test panel.
- Wire alerts: alert when regional_admit_rate drops >15% vs baseline AND token p99 increases >2x for 5m; alert for circuit_trips > 3/min; softer paging for admission_reason=memory_pressure spikes.
- Define retention and rollup: high-cardinality tags sampled and stored raw for 7 days; rollups for 30/90 day trend.

Design trade-offs considered:
- High-cardinality tags (user_id/request_id) are avoided in metrics; we use sampled traces for deep attribution.
- Sampling strategy balances debugability vs storage: 0.5% baseline + conditional higher sampling minimizes blind spots during incidents.
- We will not instrument token-level timings synchronously on the hot path; use an async batching agent to emit timing events to reduce on-path overhead.

Deliverables:
1) Instrumentation PR with metrics and trace enrichment (backend + runtime hook).
2) Grafana dashboard JSON and provisioning.
3) Alerting rules (PagerDuty thresholds + runbook links).
4) Short playbook for on-call: how to interpret the dashboard and execute region failover or admission tuning.

Links: Grafana draft: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/adm-kpi/token-path-trace-draft, Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RISLO/Admission+KPIs+and+Token+Path+Tracing, Runbook draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-admission-playbook, Engineering PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5873
acceptance_criteria: All listed metrics emitted with correct tags and pass unit tests
Sampled token-path traces available in tracing UI with stage-level timings for >=95% of sampled traces
Grafana dashboard deployed to staging and matches mock panels in design doc
Alerting rules created with test alerts firing in staging and runbook linked
End-to-end synthetic test demonstrating cross-region admission delta and proper alerting
comments: 2026-03-02 — Initial spike found that KV hit tagging required a small runtime change to avoid extra memory copy. Miguel will land a micro-optimizing patch to emit a boolean kv_prefix_hit tag.
2026-03-05 — Decided to keep baseline sampling at 0.5% to contain storage growth; increased conditional sample for latency/admit-reject events to 5% (agreed with SRE).
2026-03-09 — UX review: consolidated admit/reject reasons into stable enum to reduce cardinality. DES lead suggested color-coding heatmap by shard density.
2026-03-11 — PR #5873 opened for runtime hooks. Benchmarks show async emit adds ~0.3ms p50 on request path — acceptable.
2026-03-13 — Deployed dashboard to staging. Noted a gap: regional_admit_rate uses old metric name; patching exporter to publish admit_rate_v2.
notes: Operator-facing panels should prioritize time-to-action: admission_rate, admit_reasons, token p99 by stage, and circuit_trips (top-left).
Plan to reuse parts of existing failover synthetic harness (ENG-48888) to drive the dashboard during drills.
Coordinate with product to ensure any public-facing SLO language is not changed by these internal telemetry improvements.
